UCF vs Iowa State prediction Beating Iowa State is pretty simple: Contain Aiden Flora, and you've got 'em. The third-year sophomore has five games in which he's gone over 100 yards. In those games, his lowest output was 182 yards in a 42-31 defense-optional shootout against Baylor two weeks ago. The Cyclones are 4-0 in those other games, three of which saw Flora surpass 200 yards on the ground. He's racked up a ridiculous 619 yards and six touchdowns over the past three games, adding eight catches for 58 yards as well as a pair of pass completions (only one went for anything, a 37-yarder last week vs. Cincinnati). UCF's run defense ranks eighth in the 16-team Big 12 at just under 137 yards per game. They held Arizona State to 3.6 yards per carry last week but surrendered nearly 5 ypc and four touchdowns to Kansas in a winning effort the week prior. Arkansas State transfer Jaylen Raynor has led the Big 12's worst passing offense at just under 207 yards per game, but even he's played better in recent weeks amid Flora's ascension, throwing for 794 yards and six TDs against just two interceptions. The Knights can absolutely win on Senior Night. The run game was stifled by Arizona State, but UCF was without lead back Duke Watson, and Iowa State has the third-worst run-stopping unit in the Big 12. If everyone is back and healthy, and if Alonza Barnett can complement that with some timely strikes, the Knights can get the win. The Cyclones haven't won any of their four road games this season, but three of those teams (Iowa, BYU and Arizona) are ranked. A bowl berth might come down to the final week, just like it did in 2023. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 12 Preview: Iowa State Cyclones @ UCF Knights | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 18, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Big 12 UCF and Iowa State battle for bowl eligibility at the Bounce House, while Aiden Flora is on a hot streak. Time and date: Friday, November 20 at 6:00 p.m. ET Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: UCF (-2.5) Over/under: 49.5 All-time series: Iowa State leads, 1-0 Last meeting: Iowa State 38, UCF 35 — October 19, 2024 Current streak: Iowa State, 1 (2024) Setting the scene Friday night football kicks off early this week. At 6 p.m. ET, the Bounce House welcomes Iowa State for the first time as two 5-5 Big 12 opponents compete for bowl eligibility. UCF has been the master of chaotic finishes this season, recently shocking BYU in double overtime and upending Kansas with a game-winning touchdown on the final snap. Iowa State has also escaped a handful of close finishes this year, sliding past West Virginia in a back-and-forth finish before kicking a game-winning field goal on Halloween to upset Oklahoma State. With two teams accustomed to close finishes chasing that coveted sixth win, and a potential Heisman finisher involved, Friday night in Orlando should feature no shortage of drama. Iowa State Cyclones outlook Iowa State (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) has been as battle-tested as anyone in college football this season. The Cyclones already faced four teams ranked in the top 20 of the latest College Football Playoff rankings. They’ve also defeated three Big 12 opponents with records of 5-5 or greater, eking out close wins over West Virginia and Oklahoma State before blowing the doors of Cincinnati last Saturday. There have been two different versions of the Cyclones in year one under Jimmy Rogers. In Ames, Iowa State is a force to be reckoned with, posting a 5-1 home record with a lone defeat to No. 2 Utah. Yet, the Cyclones remain in search of their first road victory under Rogers, although all four of their road opponents are currently 6-4 or better. Iowa State’s success is largely correlated with the performance of Doak Walker Award semifinalist Aiden Flora. The running back has catapulted into the No. 1 spot on the nation’s rushing leaderboard at 1,335 yards, thanks to three consecutive 180+ yard explosions. Flora has an FBS-best five 180-yard games this year, including three performances where he eclipsed 210 yards. The versatile sophomore is a touchdown machine, and his scoring ability isn’t limited to just the run game. In addition to producing 12 rushing touchdowns, Flora has thrown two passing touchdowns and recorded a punt return touchdown, and he also ranks second on the team in receptions. The explosive Flora has four 60-yard runs this year, a total topped by just three FBS programs. His ability opens up things for the passing game, which has a commensalistic relationship with the future All-Big 12 running back. All three of Jaylen Raynor’s 250-yard showings through the air occurred when Flora crossed 180 on the ground. The mobile quarterback has been able to stretch the field more vertically as of late. He has started 10 games this season, yet 42 percent of his passing yards and 46 percent of his passing touchdowns occurred in the last three weeks. Raynor has established a strong connection with true freshman Jamal Polite Jr., who averages 19.5 yards per reception as the premier downfield threat. But what happens when Flora goes under 180? Iowa State has struggled when it gets behind the sticks. The Cyclones are 113th nationally in third down offense, and Iowa State has converted just 20-of-71 (28.2 percent) third downs across its five losses. The Cyclones have been inconsistent on defense. They enjoyed strong performances against BYU and Cincinnati but allowed at least 39 points in four of their last six contests. Iowa State ranks 108th in total defense, struggling particularly against the run where it allows 174 yards per game on a 4.93 average. Inside linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has been one of the unit’s key playmakers, checking in at third in the Big 12 with 93 tackles. However, the Cyclones are severely lacking in two categories on defense: sacks and interceptions. They rank 100th in the FBS with 1.6 sacks per game, and defensive end Isaac Terrell leads the unit with 3.5 — producing three of those sacks in the Sept. 5 opener. Additionally, Iowa State has only picked off two passes all season, and two were courtesy of middle linebacker Beau Goodwin. Thus, the secondary looks to make more havoc plays and avoid these high-scoring shootout style games moving forward. UCF Knights outlook UCF (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) is on the brink of its second bowl appearance since joining the Big 12 in 2023. The Knights are the last remaining program that has yet to produce a winning record as a member of the conference, but the opportunity to end the drought presents itself this November. Since stunning then-No. 2 BYU in overtime on Oct. 24, the Knights are 0-2 at home, dropping lopsided contests to Baylor and Arizona State. All four of UCF’s Big 12 losses came by at least 10 points, while all three wins were by single-digits, as the Knights have shown the ability to prosper in tightly-contested games. To qualify for bowl eligibility, UCF must jumpstart its offense which has scored 22 points across its last two games at the Bounce House. The Knights recently returned to their original starting quarterback Alonza Barnett III, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2 at Pittsburgh. Barnett has won 13 of his last 16 starts, and the senior has elevated the passing attack, surpassing 250 passing yards in both starts this November. Barnett’s presence on the field has turned wide receiver Josh Derry into a budding star. In his past two games, Derry has hauled in 15 receptions for 280 yards and a touchdown, emerging as the top receiver in this offense. True freshman Tyren Hornes is also making strides, registering 59 receiving yards (his second-highest total of the season) and his second career touchdown against the Sun Devils. However, the Knights must improve their pass protection, as they rank 113th nationally with 2.7 sacks allowed per game. That correlates to an unsatisfying third down conversion rate of 34.4 percent, which sits one spot below Iowa State on the national leaderboard. But perhaps the greatest struggle for UCF’s offense — which is also related to the offensive line — is the decline of the run game. The Knights haven’t produced a 100-yard rusher since Week 3, or a 60-yard rusher in each of their last three games. No UCF running back has rattled off a 20-yard run since Oct. 24, and the Knights look to create lanes for Duke Watson, Landen Chambers, and Taevion Swint to break that streak. The Knights are typically strong starters on defense, and they have yet to allow more than seven points in a first quarter this season. However, finishing games is a priority for a unit that allowed 25 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Kansas and 27 unanswered in the final 20 minutes against Houston. UCF continues to operate without one of its top defenders in strong safety Demari Henderson, who suffered an injury late in the BYU game on Oct. 24. Still, there is veteran talent across the secondary including cornerback Antione Jackson, whose 10 pass breakups lead the Big 12, and cornerback Jayden Williams, who ranks second on the team with 53 tackles, in addition to recording one interception and two forced fumbles. While the Knights are better than the Cyclones in turnover production, they similarly struggle in getting to opposing quarterbacks. Defensive end Isaiah Nixon leads UCF with 2.5 sacks on the season, and the team has gone consecutive weeks without registering a sack. Despite the offenses trending in different directions, UCF opens as a slight favorite over Iowa State, largely due to the location of the game. The Knights recorded two of their three Big 12 wins at the Bounce House, while the Cyclones have been futile away from home this year. The plamayking of Aiden Flora will be the main determinant in this matchup. Flora recorded over 100 rushing yards and three touchdowns in the first quarter last week, almost single-handedly putting Cincinnati away in 15 minutes. UCF’s defense must be prepared to counter the running back in any way possible. Stacking the box isn’t always an ideal strategy, because Iowa State loves to catch defenses off-guard with his pop passes. The Cyclones will keep things creative on offense, and UCF must remain disciplined defensively beyond the first quarter. Iowa State sustains its offensive rhythm from the last three weeks, while the Knights struggle to find openings for their run game. The end result: the Cyclones become bowl eligible in Jimmy Rogers’ debut season. The Huskers get their shot against Ohio State in Lincoln on Senior Day. It’s the last home game of the year, and a win would change how a lot of fans feel about this season. On the Carriker Chronicles, Adam Carriker breaks down why Nebraska has a chance, what worries him most, and why he thinks this game could still be up for grabs in the fourth quarter. Nebraska’s shutout of Rutgers showed how good this defense can be. The running game also put together a complete performance, which gives the Huskers something to build on. But can they run the ball against Ohio State when the Buckeyes know it’s coming? Carriker wants Nebraska to run with a purpose and give Anthony Colandrea some quick answers in the passing game. Get the tight ends involved. Take a few shots downfield when the matchup is there. And when it’s third down, give Ohio State something it hasn’t already seen. At some point, somebody has to win a one-on-one matchup. The biggest question on defense is Jeremiah Smith. How does Rob Aurich keep a receiver that good from taking over the game? That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. A couple of big plays can undo an otherwise good afternoon for the defense. The Huskers need to keep Smith from getting loose and give themselves a chance to get off the field on third down. The 7-3 Buckeyes climbed six spots to No. 14 in Tuesday’s playoff rankings , just outside the top 12. Lincoln is a tough place for that test. McElroy pointed out that opponents convert just under 24% of their third downs against Nebraska. That puts more of the load on Jeremiah Smith, the Heisman Trophy betting favorite with 1,317 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns. Nebraska’s kicking is another worry, since the Huskers are 6 of 13 on field goals. Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

home.headline: Andrew Marshall injury could keep Nebraska from taking the next step in evolution
home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. picks.blurb: The latest odds for Wisconsin vs. Purdue paint a sad reality for Luke Fickell Skip to main content About Us Wisconsin Badgers News Wisconsin Football Wisconsin Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Wisconsin Badgers In The Pros Wisconsin Football Recruiting Wisconsin Football All-Time Lists Wisconsin Basketball Recruiting Wisconsin Women's Basketball Wisconsin Basketball All-Time Lists The Wisconsin Badgers were terrible against the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday. There's no other way to slice it or dice it, it was disgraceful at best and a 'fire everybody in the whole football department' at worst. Which is what many of the Wisconsin fans are calling for. Maryland had only one Big Ten game all season and had fired their head coach. The Terrapins are a basement-dwelling Big Ten team. So, what does Vegas do for Wisconsin when the Badgers take on another basement-dwelling team, Purdue? Well, they give them barely favorable odds. Can't trust them. The best thing Wisconsin has going for itself in this Purdue game is that it's the Boilermakers that the Terrapins beat a couple of games ago. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. away.blurb: As we do each week, here's how each offensive position group graded out in the loss. Hopkins certainly deserves criticism for his performance, but offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes' questionable play-calling and an inconsistent rushing attack did little to put him in an ideal position to succeed. Darrion Dupree handled the bulk of the workload, rushing 14 times for 57 yards (4.1 YPC) and two scores while adding four receptions for 21 yards. The junior was responsible for both Wisconsin touchdowns, scoring from four yards out in the first quarter and punching in a one-yard run early in the fourth. However, his third-quarter fumble proved devastating, handing Maryland possession deep in Wisconsin territory and setting up a touchdown that gave the Terrapins their first lead. The offensive line's continued inability to establish consistent running lanes complicates the evaluation, and Dupree had his share of positive moments. Nevertheless, his costly turnover and the group's limited overall production prevent a higher grade. Sama's lack of touches was difficult to understand, and his role in the offense moving forward will be worth monitoring. Hilton continues to show flashes of considerable potential, making his limited production particularly frustrating. That general sentiment can be applied to the receiving corps as a whole, which has struggled to establish any consistency amid the offense's recurring dysfunction. Wisconsin's tight ends offered little in the passing game and continued to struggle as blockers, making this one of the offense's most disappointing position groups. Ryan Schwendeman was involved in a botched fourth-and-short exchange in the first quarter that resulted in a lost fumble, although the official scoring charged Hopkins with the turnover. The decision to hand the ball to Schwendeman rather than a running back or attempt a quarterback sneak was another questionable call from Grimes. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. away.blurb: A potential two-month recovery timeline could put Avdalas in position to return around January, although North Carolina has not announced a specific return date. Updated Wednesday morning, 11-18-2026 Clemson (12 out) and Duke (11) have the first Week 12… North Carolina's Neo Avdalas to Miss Two Months With Wrist Injury Football North Carolina basketball has suffered a significant setback early in the 2026-27 season, as sophomore guard Neo Avdalas is expected to miss approximately two months after suffering a fractured left wrist. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. Through North Carolina’s first four games, Avdalas averaged 9.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and a team-leading 3.8 assists per game. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. His absence will be an early test for Malone and the Tar Heels as they attempt to maintain momentum and navigate the opening portion of their ACC schedule without one of their key offseason additions. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their picks for college football's biggest matchups of the weekend Getty Images Call college football's Week 12 schedule a breather if you want to -- just keep that same energy again Saturday night when there are a handful of results we never saw coming. There isn't a single AP Top 25 matchup on the schedule, but 10 ranked teams are single-digit favorites on the road. How many of them are you willing to trust with their College Football Playoff seeding and potential conference title hopes on the line? This is the kind of slate that looks harmless until a favorite trails by a couple of touchdowns early or starts feeling the heat in the second half of a game that could go in either direction. We're picking the biggest games of Week 12, including a few where the road favorite might spend Sunday figuring out how much damage one afternoon did to its résumé. Season results : Brad Crawford (67-34 straight up, 45-55-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (73-28 straight up, 50–50-1 ATS) We're in a futile state of affairs, folks. I'm afraid the hole is too deep for me to crawl out of this season to continue my winning streak against Hummer in our annual head-to-head picks battle. We both had losing records last week, but he still picked up a game on me and now holds a five-game lead with a couple of weekends left. No. 14 Ohio State (-3.5) at Nebraska Hummer ( Ohio State -3.5): These are two good and flawed teams. Both are top 20 defenses. Both have largely struggled on offense since mid-October. An injury to Julian Sayin caused Ohio State's issues. Tougher competition caught up to the Huskers. I just don't see Nebraska moving the ball all that well against the Buckeyes. Luke Fahey has played pretty well the last two weeks. He and the Buckeyes' offense do enough. … Ohio State 27, Nebraska 21. Crawford (Ohio State -3.5): Y'all know Matt Rhule's record against top-25 opponents, right? I can keep things short here if so. The Buckeyes still have an outside shot at getting in the CFP discussion as a bubble team with convincing wins this week and next (against Michigan ). Jeremiah Smith needs a monster outing on the road to remain in the frontrunner discussion for the Heisman. He has scored in seven straight games but is no longer the first player voters think of when top players are mentioned. ... Ohio State 27, Nebraska 20. No. 10 BYU (-6.5) at Kansas Hummer ( BYU -6.5): Kansas is an odd team. The Jayhawks are top 45 nationally in both yards per play and yards allowed per play. But they're also just 2-5 in the Big 12 and have struggled with both turnovers and injuries. The problem for Kansas is that it can struggle to stop the run, and that's what BYU does best. I could see this being close. But I'll take the team with a lot on the line that's been incredibly consistent this season. … BYU 31, Kansas 24. Crawford (BYU -6.5): At 4-6 overall this season, the Jayhawks need consecutive wins over BYU and Oklahoma State to reach bowl eligibility. It's not going to come to fruition, unfortunately. BYU has to win and look good doing it to avoid dropping in the CFP rankings, and there's no margin for error in the conference title discussion behind Utah and Texas Tech . BYU does not control its own destiny, but if the Cougars win out, they're going to have a strong argument for inclusion. ... BYU 34, Kansas 20. No. 15 Iowa (-6.5) at Illinois Hummer ( Iowa -6.5): The Illini are a better team than some of the advanced stats would suggest, largely because their defense did a 180 after a coordinator change. But the Hawkeyes are the better overall team, especially if they get decent quarterback play from Hank Brown . Iowa should control the lines of scrimmage and the general pace of the game. The only thing that could flip that is turnovers, which is something that Iowa's struggled with in losses this season. But the Hawkeyes get it done. … Iowa 27, Illinois 20. Crawford (Iowa -6.5): Can Katin Houser put the Fighting Illini in position to win this one against a defense that rarely gives up big plays? He's coming off a three-interception game against UCLA , but has been solid for the most part throughout the campaign with 18 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Iowa's playing with stakes in this one, with a chance to finish 10-2 overall by winning out. Morgan leads the team with 525 receiving yards and 41 receptions while being second on the team with three touchdowns. Morgan spoke with the media on Monday where he spoke his mind on the matchup with his former team. “It’s a nice big stadium, older fans, so it’s not that loud, so we’re gonna have fun.” Morgan said. “The process is a process, and we got to keep going what we did to come this far,” Morgan said. “We don’t want to change the process based on our opponent. But it is kind of a special thing for me. I spent some time there, won a championship there, so it is going to be nice going back there. But I don’t want to overthink about it. I just want to keep the process.” Over his three seasons in Ann Arbor, Morgan posted 566 receiving yards and scored six touchdowns. Four of those touchdowns came in the 2023 championship season, with Morgan tying for the fourth-most touchdowns on the team with future first round pick Colston Loveland. Morgan’s most successful season with the Wolverines coming in 2025, racking up 223 yards and averaging 11.2 yards per reception. away.headline: Michigan football another underdog vs. UCLA, with a season-low point total
away.blurb: To little surprise, Michigan football will be another underdog when it returns home to play No. 4 UCLA this Saturday. Oddsmakers currently list the Wolverines as 5.5 to 6.5-point underdogs for the team’s final home game of the 2026 season (3:30 p.m., CBS). Numbers vary across the market, with BetMGM , DraftKings and Caesars currently showing Michigan +5.5, while FanDuel has Michigan +6.5. That number is smaller than Saturday’s game at Oregon, where the Wolverines opened as nearly two-touchdown underdogs before closing as 10-point underdogs. Michigan lost, 31-7, to the Ducks after another poor showing offensively. Michigan (5-5, 2-5 Big Ten) has failed to cover the spread in three straight games and six of its last seven, another sign of struggle for Kyle Whittingham’s team. As things stand currently, oddsmakers have also set a season-low point total for Saturday’s game, with books ranging from 37.5 to 39.5. Michigan’s had three games close with a total of 39.5 this season, including the last two. Eight of the Wolverines’ 10 games this season have gone under the closing total, aided by Michigan’s 131st-ranked offense. Michigan’s opponent on Saturday, UCLA, is 10-0 under first-year coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins held off Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night to stay unbeaten, but it was the first time all season they failed to cover the spread. Yes, UCLA is 9-1 against the spread this season, overachieving expectations across the board, even from oddsmakers. Six of the Bruins’ 10 games have also gone under the total. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit mlive.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

away.headline: Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit
away.blurb: He did not come out with the rest of the team out of halftime and did not return to the game to start the third quarter. UCLA's backup quarterback is Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava. He's in his second season with the Bruins and has seen limited action in his college career. Ty Dieffenbach injury updates: UCLA QB returns after exiting in first half after hard hit - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Jordan Mendoza, USA TODAY · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 14, 2026 at 3:53 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PASADENA, CA — UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury on a hard hit late in the first half against Illinois on Friday, Nov. 13. But it appears to not be an absolutely devastating hit for the Bruins . With 35 seconds left in the second quarter, Dieffenbach tried to throw the ball away when he got tripped up and was clearly in immediate pain. He was visibly shaken as he was attended to by support staff, and he appeared to indicate he had a left shoulder injury. After a few minutes he was helped up and taken to the sideline. Once the teams headed to the locker room, Dieffenbach went in appearing to not move his left arm and was limping. Ty Dieffenbach latest injury news Dieffenbach suffered an "upper body injury," according to the Fox broadcast. However, he emerged from the locker room with about four minutes left in the third quarter with a sleeve on his left arm, as the Rose Bowl crowd cheered. Dieffenbach was back on the field for UCLA late in the third quarter and played the remainder of the game. "I kind of went down a little awkward on the tackle, and my arm got caught up underneath, but it just got a little tight on me, and it's nothing serious," he said postgame. The Bruins got their quarterback to engineer another win. He reignited the offense, throwing a key fourth quarter touchdown to Semaj Morgan that strengthened the lead. UCLA held on to beat Illinois 22-14 to move to 10-0. Dieffenbach went 13-for-20 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, with 28 rushing yards. The injury was a big scare to UCLA's quarterback room as Dieffenbach has played in place of starter Nico Iamaleava after Iamaleava suffered a season ending injury against Oregon on Oct. 10. Dieffenbach has stepped up and kept the Bruins one of two undefeated teams left in the country, at 9-0 for the first time since 1998 with a shot at their first College Football Playoff appearance. Prior to the injury, Dieffenbach was 8-for-13 for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception, leading UCLA to a 10-0 lead over Illinois. home.headline: Oregon vs. Michigan State injury report reveals more Ducks injuries and a major Spartans dilemma
home.blurb: Given that Oregon faces off against Michigan State on Friday Night , the initial injury report for this matchup came out a day sooner, with the schedule being pushed up a day. On Tuesday Night, the first injury report revealed the status of Jordon Davison, Douglas Utu, Jerry Mixon, Bear Alexander, and, surprisingly, Michigan State backup QB Cam Fancher. The best news for the Oregon Ducks was that offensive lineman Douglas Utu did not appear on the first injury report. The veteran guard missed time in the second half with what appeared to be a leg injury, but it appears that he'll return to the lineup this weekend. Defensive Tackle Bear Alexander appeared to have suffered an ankle injury vs. Michigan, but he returned to the game and is probable for Friday Night's matchup. Where the concerns start for Dan Lanning's group is with the status of linebacker Jerry Mixon, who missed the Michigan game. It was stated that Jerry Mixon tweaked something in warmups for the showdown with the Wolverines, but based on the fact that he's doubtful for this weekend's game, it appears to be more serious than a simple tweak. Even more disappointing is the status of Jordon Davison, who's been out since the first half of the Northwestern game. Dan Lanning shared that Davison was out of his walking boot, but he won't return to the field this weekend, putting all eyes on the showdown with the Huskies to end the season. Milivojevic remains out. Making matters more concerning for the Spartans is the fact that backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed as questionable, as they could be forced to turn to their third-string QB against a stout Oregon defense. As the week goes on, the Spartans side of the report is going to be important to follow with 7 players listed as questionable, which can truly go either way. The good news for Oregon is that they're far from the only team dealing with serious injury issues, but it's also disappointing to see how many teams have been knocked down a level with all these injuries. The Oregon Ducks head into the final two games of the regular season looking to build on the momentum of this three-game winning streak, and to continue making a case for a College Football Playoff bid. Among the two teams standing in the Ducks' way are the Michigan State Spartans with a 3-7 record this season. While the Spartans have struggled, anything can happen in college football, and as Oregon continues to be plagued with injuries, the Ducks continue to dig deeper into the depth chart. This weekend, Dan Lanning and the Ducks will likely look across to the opposing sideline, and see that they're not alone dealing with rampant injuries. home.headline: Michigan State injury report: QB Milivojevic out; 7 questionable
home.blurb: Starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic is listed as out for Michigan State against No. 14 Oregon on the availability report released by the Big Ten on Nov. 17. Backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed as questionable. Updates to the report are due the next two days before a final report two hours before Friday's 8 p.m. kickoff. In total, 10 Michigan State players are listed out, and seven are listed questionable, which is an improvement from 12 players listed out a week ago. Among those listed out are safety Devin Vaught, linebacker Jordan Hall, tight end Jayden Savoury, and defensive tackle Ben Roberts, the latter who reaggravated a knee injury after two snaps against Washington in a 21-14 loss Nov. 14. For Oregon, outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti is among eight players listed out. Inside linebacker Jerry Mixon is questionable, while defensive lineman Bear Alexander is probable. Also out for the Ducks remains Detroit King alumnus Dante Moore, who has not played since being hit while going down for a slide in a Sept. 26 win over Southern Cal. Milivojevic (left arm) will miss his second game of the season. He was unavailable for an Oct. 24 loss to UCLA at the Rose Bowl, where true freshman Kayd Coffman made his first career start. The East Kentwood product might start again if Fancher (right knee) cannot play. Coffman threw completions on his first four passes including a touchdown, but has since thrown seven incompletions including an interception. Alongside Fancher, wide receiver Rodney Bullard Jr., running back Jaziun Patterson, cornerback Tre Bell, nickelback Michael Richard, left guard Conner Moore and tight end Brennan Parachek are listed as questionable. Bell was a game-time decision against Washington but did not play. Moore injured his right knee one snap before Milivojevic's injury, while Richard went down in the second half and did not return. The story of Michigan State’s football season could be told through its injury report. Its best summary is the data: Out of 42 players to start at least one game, 13 of them are out or questionable accounting for a combined 80 starts out of 220 as a team. On offense, Michigan State is missing 1,559 snaps, 20 percent of its season total. On defense, 2,657 missing snaps account for a loss of 40 percent. This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Michigan State injury report: QB Milivojevic out; 7 questionable Michigan State could be down to a true freshman quarterback once again when Oregon comes to Spartan Stadium this week. Michigan State (3-7, 1-6 Big Ten) is a 14 1/2-point underdog to Oregon (7-3, 5-2), which ESPN Analytics gives an 86.4 percent chance to win.

Tennessee's College Football Playoff hopes are on the line this weekend against LSU. If the Vols beat LSU on Saturday in Neyland Stadium, they'll just need a win in the regular-season finale against Vanderbilt to lock down a spot in the College Football Playoff. But if Tennessee loses to LSU, they can likely kiss their playoff hopes goodbye. LSU, which has four losses, is out of the playoff picture. The Tigers' 6-4 record, however, isn't indicative of how good of a team they are. LSU has arguably the most talented roster in the nation, and they are just a couple of plays away from being 8-2. Combine that with the fact that Tennessee will be without several key players against the Tigers — specifically left guard Nic Moore and wide receiver Mike Matthews — and it's easy to see why there's some concern about this game on Rocky Top. Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray makes his prediction for LSU vs Tennessee Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray predicted last week that Tennessee would beat Texas A&M by 13 points last week (the Vols won by 15 points), but he's not making the same kind of prediction for the LSU game. Murray has the Tigers taking down the Vols on Saturday, predicting that LSU will leave Neyland Stadium with a 23-17 win. One of the main reasons Murray is predicting an LSU win is because the Vols will be without Mike Matthews. “This (LSU) defense is going to be able to put you in third-and-long situations,” said Murray. “And they're going to be able to get to the quarterback with Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross coming off the edge. “… Can Tennessee's offense, without Matthews and with a banged up quarterback — it's possibly Faizon Brandon back in there playing quarterback — get the job done against LSU in this matchup? I don't feel very confident. Which is why I'm going with LSU 23-17 in this football game. If Mike Matthews was healthy, and if [George MacIntyre] — I don't know what the knee is right now, maybe he's 100 percent for the game [and I would feel different]. But still, no Mike Matthews. I think that's a big problem for the Tennessee Volunteers. So I think LSU wins the game.” I think that's a fair prediction from Murray. There are certainly questions about the Vols' offense without Matthews. The junior wide receiver was easily Tennessee's most dynamic playmaker. But LSU has failed to finish games in the fourth quarter this season and that's an area where Tennessee has thrived. If the Vols can get this game to the fourth quarter, I like their chances. But if they get to the fourth quarter and they're down multiple scores, it could be too big of a hill for Tennessee's offense to climb. ‘I know in that room' – The biggest reason the CFP committee is giving for ranking Alabama so high will make Tennessee fans even more mad The Tennessee Volunteers dropped one spot in the College Football Playoff rankings this week despite their road win over the Texas A&M Aggies. ‘Months of rehab' – Vols insider gives the latest on WR Mike Matthews and whether he could be back at Tennessee in 2027 Tennessee Volunteers wide receiver Mike Matthews will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a season-ending knee injury against the Texas A&M Aggies this past weekend. Longhorns have the ball but if you're an LSU fan, your defense is the unit you want on the field to try and close this game out. Tigers have limited Texas to just 217 yards of offense and have forced three turnovers. Slowly but surely, Texas is getting back into this game as Gianni Spetic knocks in his third field goal of the game. He knocked this one in from 50 yards out to shrink LSU's lead to just five points. The Tigers have been living and dying in the air for the most part of this game until running back Dillin Jones found a lane. Jones broke out for a 44-yard rushing touchdown to extend LSU's lead. The run marks the longest rush of the night so far as both teams haven't run it a ton with success. That last possession of the half for LSU was a dud. Once the offense got close to the end zone, Texas' defense bowed up and LSU fizzled out. Leavitt just lobbed that ball up. I know the pressure is in his face but he's got to rifle that ball out of the back of the end zone. LSU OC Charlies Weis Jr. had Leavitt roll out plenty to avoid Texas' army of pass rushers. picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Vaughn Dalzell · NBC Sports Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:15 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame (9-1) absolutely rolled Boston College, 41-7, and all that stands between the Irish and the 12-team playoff field is SMU (7-3) and Syracuse (5-5). The Irish welcome SMU to South Bend for the regular season home finale, and that's after SMU was destroyed on senior day by Wake Forest, 49-7. The Irish will have their senior day versus SMU, so the Mustangs have the chance to be party crashers. However, if there's any inclination to quit a second straight week after falling behind early, then SMU will get blown out again. After SMU went for it on fourth down back-to-back possessions in their own territory and failed to convert, you could see the quit. SMU turned the ball over three times, went 3-of-14 on third downs, and gave up 535 yards of offense. Notre Dame had 500 yards of offense against Boston College, with 276 of it coming on the ground. The Irish ran for 6.9 yards a pop as Jonaz Walton led the way with 141 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Micah Gilbert and Jordan Faison have both scored back-to-back games (Gilbert three-straight), and CJ Carr had his ninth game with at least 200 passing yards and eighth with two-plus touchdown passes. The defense held Boston College to a season-low 136 yards of offense, nine first downs, and 2-of-18 on third and fourth downs. The status of Charles Jagusah, who's been "out" since Summer 2025, was upgraded to off the injury report, but he'll be ready to go against the Mustangs NOTRE DAME, Ind. — The term "questionable" can carry various connotations in an injury report, depending on a player's circumstances. At least, that was the case on Monday when Notre Dame released its latest availability report ahead of Saturday's matchup with SMU. Four players were listed as questionable: offensive tackle Will Black (concussion), safety Brauntae Johnson (left foot) and defensive tackles Jason Onye (right knee) and Francis Brewu (left knee). The status of Charles Jagusah (fractured forearm), who's been "out" since Summer 2025, was upgraded to off the injury report, but he'll be ready to go against the Mustangs. Here is Notre Dame's Monday availability update ahead of SMU. Will Black is questionable with a concussion, as is Brauntae Johnson, who has been "out" since the season opener against Wisconsin. Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable after missing the last two games. https://t.co/sOIvCyx95W "He'll be similar to Brauntae," Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said of Jagusah. "His next phase of this is getting to practice and start to return to play. Let's see what he can do in practice." According to Notre Dame at the time, the initial prognosis appeared favorable for the 6-foot-5, 325-pound offensive lineman, even after a second small operation slightly pushed back his return timeline from late September to October. Only, a fall return never materialized, as he endured at least three more procedures to address an infection that prevented the injury from properly healing. "Once his bone heals and his muscles are strong, we'll enter into the return-to-play side of things." His return-to-play protocol finally began this fall, and he began rebuilding strength after missing a year of opportunities to train his upper body. "That doesn't mean he can go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week, and that is huge," Freeman said. "Oh man, that's amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice." "Something crazy I just found out is that he's never played a game in Notre Dame Stadium," Freeman said. "He's played in a couple games, but he's never stepped on the field in a game in Notre Dame Stadium, and if he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? "But his journey has been amazing in terms of the things he's overcome. I'm so excited to see that guy out in practice this week." picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 18, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. BLACKSBURG — After a 23-point loss to SMU in Dallas, Virginia Tech football takes on Stanford in a Saturday night showdown in Lane Stadium. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Wright, Austin, Bright, Terry) Wide Receiver: 2 (Peterkin, Stuewe) Virginia Tech (6-3, 3-3 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) and Boston College (21-14). The Hokies claimed their largest margin of victory since 1922 with their 70-point win over the Keydets Sept. 5, and they avenged their loss from Sept. 13, 2025, against the Monarchs which forced the ouster of then-head coach — and Virginia Tech's current defensive coordinator/linebackers coach — Brent Pry one day later. Against Maryland, the Hokies broke a 15-game Power Four non-conference losing streak dating back to 2017, beating the Terrapins by nine. Sept. 26's victory in Boston College was harder to come by, but amid a nor'easter, sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s career-high 209 rushing yards proved enough for the Hokies to escape with the victory. The Hokies sustained their first loss on Oct. 2, falling to Pitt 35-33 after conceding a 35-10 run over two-plus quarters. Virginia Tech made a nine-point rally to pull within two, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard field goal attempt for the win was ruled no good. The Hokies lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley the following week, ceding the game-winning touchdown to the Golden Bears with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech returned to the win column on Oct. 17, defeating Georgia Tech 34-24 in a contest where it led 24-3 at intermission. The Hokies then became bowl eligible with a 20-16 win over Clemson — their first over the Tigers since 2007 in their trip to Memorial Stadium since 2012. Virginia Tech, however, fell in a 51-28 blowout at SMU Nov. 6, allowing season-highs in both points (51) and total yards of offense (569). The 51 points the Mustangs totaled on Virginia Tech were the most allowed by a Hokies team since the 2021 Pinstripe Bowl against Maryland, while the 569 yards Tech allowed were the most since Oct. 10, 2020, against North Carolina. However, the victory came with some concerns, particularly surrounding quarterback Jaden Craig, who appeared to be dealing with an ankle injury during the contest. READ MORE: TCU Women's Basketball Lands Two Elite Guards in 2027 Signing Class Dykes acknowledged the importance of Craig's health as TCU prepares to face an undefeated Utah team. Craig completed 20 of 34 passes for 225 yards and a touchdown against Kansas State, but his ability to move around the pocket could be affected if the ankle continues to bother him. The injury also gave sophomore Adam Schobel an opportunity to see additional playing time. With TCU still fighting to secure its postseason position, having a healthy quarterback will be particularly important against Utah's talented defense. And it seems as though Dykes believes that his starting quarterback will be ready to face off with the Utes. "Yeah, I would expect him to play," Dykes said on Tuesday. "He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him to be able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess." READ MORE: TCU gets Primetime FOX Showdown With No. 2 Utah in Fort Worth Another situation worth monitoring involves tight end Ka'Morreun Pimpton. His availability could be significant for an offense that needs as many reliable playmakers as possible against one of the country's top teams. Dykes also has plenty of reasons to be encouraged by what his team showed against Kansas State. The head coach praised the defensive performance, particularly the improvement in stopping the run and limiting explosive plays. TCU held the Wildcats to just 10 points and forced two turnovers. "Sometimes you have to win ugly and that's what we did tonight," Dykes said following the victory. That mentality could be necessary again this weekend. Utah enters the matchup ranked No. 2 nationally with a perfect 10-0 record, making the Utes arguably TCU's toughest remaining opponent. The Horned Frogs have been competitive throughout much of the season, but close losses have prevented them from putting together the record they hoped for. FORT WORTH - TCU head coach Sonny Dykes and his players expressed excitement at the challenge of facing No. 2 Utah on Saturday night at Amon G. Carter Stadium. "It's a really good Utah team," Dykes said. "They're No. 2 for a reason. They are good on offense, defense and special teams." In addition to positive words for the Utes, Dykes praised his team's energy during practice and said his players are looking forward to the challenge. "Energy was excellent today," Dykes said. "Guys were excited about practicing. We had a really good day. I think they are excited to play and looking forward to the challenge. They know it's not going to be easy. Released Wednesday, Nov. 11, unsurprisingly, the Wildcats will continue to be without quarterbacks Avery Johnson and Jacob Knuth. K-State coach Collin Klein said Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff will compete for the starting quarterback spot this week, while leaving the door open for both to play. The game kicks off on Saturday, Nov. 14, at Amon G. Carter Stadium, at 1 p.m. CT. Both teams will provide injury reports on Thursday and Friday night ahead of the game, along with one 90 minutes before Saturday's kickoff.
